# video/scripts: the tool index

<!-- generated by scripts/index.py: do not edit by hand -->
Generated by `python3 -I scripts/index.py` from each tool's own docstring or header comment, so it never drifts:
re-run it after adding, moving or re-describing a tool (`--check` exits 1 when this page is stale). Paths are from
`video/`. Usage and flags are in each tool's header; how the tools fit the gates: `docs/PIPELINE_V2.md` ("Studio
toolkit"), `docs/G5_BLOCKING.md` §4 (previews) and §7 (the gate check). v1-only tools are archived in
`archive/v1/scripts/` (the `v1-final` tag has them in place).

105 tools in 18 folders; 9 without a header (add a docstring or a first comment line).

## `scripts/`

| tool | what it does |
|---|---|
| `scripts/autocheckpoint.sh` | Periodic checkpoint (owner, 2026-10-27: "make sure to commit the progress periodically if we get stopped on the usage limits"): commits and pushes ONLY the given paths every CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL seconds (default 600) whenever they changed, so an agent stopped … |
| `scripts/camspeed.py` | on-screen SPEED and VELOCITY-CONTINUITY check of a real render (any composition: Main, S01..S13, dev). |
| `scripts/capcheck.mjs` | Caption legibility check: renders frames twice (normal + caption mask) and measures, in the caption band, how much of the background behind the text is below 3:1 contrast against the ACTIVE tone (scripts/capcheck.py). |
| `scripts/capcheck.py` | Caption legibility check (used by scripts/capcheck.mjs and scripts/sheet.sh). |
| `scripts/coreline.py` | G0.5 core line bookkeeping when the stages run as separate agents (no Workflow tool): the same maths as the G0.5 workflow templates (`context/workflows/v4-g05-facts-and-core-line-*.js`), kept in files so a usage-limit stop loses nothing. |
| `scripts/film_captions.py` | Caption pages (a hand-written paging file) + the voice's word timings -> the house CaptionBeat JSON. |
| `scripts/film_chunks.py` | The CHUNK LIST of a film for the chunked full-size render (docs/G5_BLOCKING.md §8b), one line per chunk, "idx id first last n" (the format the chunked render / join scripts read). |
| `scripts/g5_scaffold.py` | Start a video's G5 film from its locked G3 board (docs/G5_BLOCKING.md). |
| `scripts/index.py` | Write scripts/README.md, the index of every tool in video/scripts, from each tool's own header. |
| `scripts/render-frames.mjs` | Render arbitrary frames of a composition in ONE bundle + ONE browser session. |
| `scripts/render-media.mjs` | Render a composition (or a frame range of it) to a video / audio file with @remotion/renderer's renderMedia, in ONE bundle (cached while src/ and public/ are unchanged) and ONE browser (scripts/render/lib.mjs). |
| `scripts/sheet.sh` | Renders <count> frames evenly spaced over [t0, t1] seconds (one bundle, one browser) and tiles them into a labeled contact sheet (label = seconds). |
| `scripts/still.sh` | Renders one frame at <seconds> (composition time) to <out.png>; other flags go to render-frames.mjs (its cached bundle and one browser make a repeated still ~1 s). |
| `scripts/strip.sh` | Renders EVERY frame (or every Nth with --step) between t0 and t1 seconds at the composition's own fps (60 for the films; it sampled 30 fps until 2026-10-29, every 2nd frame of a 60 fps film) and tiles them with frame numbers: the tool for checking motion … |
| `scripts/topic_chart.py` | The topic shortlist as a phone-portrait column chart (owner, 2026-10-28: "show me the visual next time we do research - like the story and some bar chart ... showing the score on each category"; then "make the visual into column chart"). |

## `scripts/look/`

| tool | what it does |
|---|---|
| `scripts/look/make_blue_noise.py` | Generate the sky's blue-noise dither tile (void-and-cluster, Ulichney 1993) and print it for src/lib/sky.tsx. |
| `scripts/look/measure_camera.py` | Measure the camera language of a reference video, shot by shot (for turning reference moves into our 2D camera presets). |
| `scripts/look/palette_board.py` | House palette family: checks every palette against the house DNA and writes an HTML board (the same small scene drawn in each palette) for scripts/look/shoot.cjs to screenshot. |
| `scripts/look/shoot.cjs` | Screenshot docs/look/palette_board.html to docs/look/palette_family.png (run palette_board.py first). |
| `scripts/look/shot_sheets.py` | Contact sheets for shot-by-shot analysis: after measure_camera.py, take 3 frames per shot (10 %, 50 %, 90 % of the shot) and tile them, a fixed number of shots per sheet, labelled with shot number, time and the measured move. |
| `scripts/look/sketch_debug.py` | Side-by-side check sheets for the cinematic guidebook: each shot type's 9:16 sketch (our drawing) next to the reference frames it was translated from, so the owner can see what we index on. |
| `scripts/look/texture_shoot.cjs` | Screenshots review/look/texture/*.html to PNG (1080x1920) and motion.html to frames/ (150 frames, 30 fps). |
| `scripts/look/texture_test.py` | Texture + line test (owner, 2026-10-25): a very subtle tone-on-tone halftone on the fills, and thin tapered ink lines only in key places, vs flat and vs full outlines. |

## `scripts/qa/`

| tool | what it does |
|---|---|
| `scripts/qa/av_lag.py` | Where a reference track (the locked voice, the mix) sits inside a render's audio: the lag of the best cross-correlation per window (mono, 8 kHz) and its normalised peak r. Lag 0 ms in every window = the track plays in sync and does not drift; r ~1.0 = the … |
| `scripts/qa/beatsync.py` | How far is every cut from the music's beat grid, and a tempo map that puts beats ON the cuts. |
| `scripts/qa/calibrate.py` | Run deadframes (and framecheck) on the two reference videos and compare with the numbers the analysis streams measured by hand (docs/motion_spec.md section 9, docs/style_bible_ref2.md section 6.4). |
| `scripts/qa/check_banding.py` | BANDING in a sky (docs/look/CRAFT.md §g "Check"; lib/sky.tsx), on a rendered frame (PNG) or a video (mp4: decoded at 16 bits with its own colour tags, so the measurement adds no rounding of its own), before and after any encode. |
| `scripts/qa/check_depth.py` | The DEPTH AND SEPARATION check (docs/look/CRAFT.md §f "Check"; the owner on v2's G4 look clip, 2026-10-27: "the foreground and the main focus still blurs with the background ... no distance effect nor perspective ... the bottom part ... little to no … |
| `scripts/qa/check_light.py` | The LIGHT AND SHADOW gate (docs/look/CRAFT.md §d "Check"), on an A/B pair of the SAME frame: the light layers OFF (A) and ON (B). |
| `scripts/qa/colour_meter.py` | The COLOUR-JOB METER. |
| `scripts/qa/deadframes.py` | Find DEAD frames (nothing on screen moves once the camera is compensated), count motion EVENTS and score every scene's life 0-10. |
| `scripts/qa/density.py` | The DENSITY METER. |
| `scripts/qa/framecheck.py` | Automated per-frame sanity checks; writes the list of frames a human (or agent) should look at. |
| `scripts/qa/gate_check.py` | The scripted gate check for any film render (PIPELINE_V2 anti-waste rule 1: the mechanical checks before G6, instead of review agents). |
| `scripts/qa/master_sheets.py` | Contact sheets and join strips FROM A RENDERED MP4 (the master), time-stamped, as JPEG under a size cap; and exact full-size frames for the image checks (check_depth, check_light's B side is a PNG render, never this). |
| `scripts/qa/particles_phone.py` | The PHONE-SIZE PARTICLE TEST (CRAFT §f.6; the owner on S1's v4, 2026-10-28: "I don't see any changes in the particles anywhere"). |
| `scripts/qa/qalib.py` | Shared machinery for the QA tools in scripts/qa (deadframes, framecheck, beatsync). |
| `scripts/qa/selftest.py` | Synthetic checks that the QA tools see what they should (no rendering needed, ~1 min). |
| `scripts/qa/sheets.sh` | Frame-by-frame visual review: renders every <every_nth> frame of <CompId> between <t0> and <t1> seconds (one bundle, one browser: scripts/render-frames.mjs) and tiles them into labeled contact sheets of 6x4 = 24 frames each. |

## `scripts/qa/retro_tools/depth/`

| tool | what it does |
|---|---|
| `scripts/qa/retro_tools/depth/depth_measure.py` | Depth analysis (docs/look/research/2026-10-27_depth_analysis.md): planes, separation, ground perspective. |
| `scripts/qa/retro_tools/depth/extract_frames.sh` | The frames behind docs/look/research/2026-10-27_depth_analysis.md (run from video/; frames go to a scratch dir, never into the repo). |
| `scripts/qa/retro_tools/depth/mock_s1.py` | Pixel mock (NOT a render) of the S1 depth spec on the G4 look frame, to size the numbers: the far city mixed toward the gold band (sRGB, like dc/core mix()), optionally after a backlit shade multiply; optionally the wing's west fin in a darker material. |
| `scripts/qa/retro_tools/depth/run_compare.py` | S1 before / after: the G4 look clip (what the owner saw), the G4 look clip v2 (L1's depth pass) and the current code (a 0.4-scale still render), all measured at 432 px wide with the same boxes. |
| `scripts/qa/retro_tools/depth/run_ground.py` | Ground perspective: line directions in the lower ground region (full res 1080 wide). |
| `scripts/qa/retro_tools/depth/run_planes.py` | Per-plane colour, contrast and detail (near -> far), with the air colour behind the farthest plane. |
| `scripts/qa/retro_tools/depth/run_scale.py` | Size gradient: px per metre of things of known size against their base's height below the horizon, and the eye ratio (feet y - horizon) / height of people (one camera = one ratio per ground plane). |
| `scripts/qa/retro_tools/depth/run_sep.py` | Silhouette separation: the subject (or a near mass) against what is right behind it. |

## `scripts/qa/retro_tools/hierarchy/`

| tool | what it does |
|---|---|

| `scripts/qa/retro_tools/hierarchy/motion2.py` | Motion v2: every burst frame aligned to the mid frame (ECC affine, full 540 res, chained init), blur s=1, consecutive aligned diffs; 'edge residual' killed by an opening (3x3) + threshold. |
| `scripts/qa/retro_tools/hierarchy/sheet.py` | Contact sheet of mid frames with a 10 % grid for picking subject boxes. |
| `scripts/qa/retro_tools/hierarchy/tiers.py` | Per-tier look at 1080 wide: subject box / Pip / foreground band (bottom 28 %, outside the subject) / environment. |
